The Buying Process: What to Expect

New Lamborghini Purchase

Buying a new Lamborghini in 2026 involves navigating a market where demand for most models exceeds supply. Here's what to expect:

  1. Configuration — Work with the dealer's brand specialist to specify your car via Lamborghini's Ad Personam customization program. Choices include exterior color (standard and Ad Personam options), interior material and color, wheel design, and numerous performance and comfort options
  2. Order placement — The dealer submits your order to Lamborghini headquarters; allocation is managed centrally based on dealer volume and customer priority
  3. Wait time — For the Revuelto, expect 12-18 months. For the Urus S, 3-9 months is more typical. The Huracán Tecnica is increasingly available from stock as the model approaches end of production
  4. Delivery deposit — Typically 10-15% of MSRP, paid at order placement
  5. Final payment — On delivery; financing arranged through Lamborghini Financial Services or your own bank

Pre-Owned Purchase

The pre-owned process is more straightforward but requires due diligence:

  1. Carfax and service records review — Non-negotiable; a complete service history from authorized dealers is strongly preferred
  2. Pre-purchase inspection (PPI) — Have an independent Lamborghini-specialist technician inspect the car, particularly if buying from a private party
  3. Title verification — Ensure clean title with no liens; use a title search service for private purchases
  4. Test drive — Request a test drive on a mix of highway and city roads; listen for unusual sounds from the engine, transmission, and suspension

Negotiation Tips for Miami Lamborghini Buyers

Lamborghinis are not heavily negotiated in the way that mainstream vehicles are, but there are strategies that create value:

  • New cars: don't negotiate on price, negotiate on allocation — In a seller's market for the Revuelto, asking for a price discount rarely works. Instead, focus on getting earlier delivery, better allocation priority, or included options
  • Pre-owned: everything is negotiable — Dealers have more flexibility on used inventory, particularly if a car has been sitting for more than 60 days. Research comparable sales on Bring a Trailer and duPont REGISTRY before making an offer
  • CPO premium is negotiable — The CPO certification premium (typically $10,000–$25,000 above market) can often be reduced, particularly for cars approaching the program's age or mileage limits
  • Trade-in leverage — If you have a trade-in, get an independent appraisal from a separate dealer before accepting the selling dealer's offer. Trade-in value is a common area where dealers recoup flexibility on sale price
  • Year-end timing — The final quarter of the calendar year often brings more dealer flexibility as they manage inventory and quota targets. December and January can be advantageous for pre-owned purchases
  • Build relationships — Miami's Lamborghini community is tight-knit. Dealers reward repeat customers and referrals with allocation priority and better service. If you're a first-time buyer, buying a CPO Urus before ordering a Revuelto is a recognized pathway to priority treatment

Final Advice for Miami Lamborghini Buyers

Miami is one of the best cities in the world to own a Lamborghini. The climate is perfect for open-air driving, the roads (particularly the MacArthur and Venetian causeways) provide genuine spectacle, and the social context — where a Lamborghini is noticed and appreciated rather than provoking resentment — makes every drive an event.

For new buyers: start with a test drive at both The Collection and Prestige Imports. Compare the buying experiences, the inventory, and the personalities of the brand specialists. The relationship you form with your dealer matters over time, particularly as you consider future purchases or trades. Choose the one that treats you best.

For the market as a whole: Lamborghini ownership in Miami has never been more accessible (relatively speaking) or more supported. The brand's dealer network, service infrastructure, and community of local owners creates an ecosystem that makes the ownership experience genuinely rewarding. Welcome to the herd.
